questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in English, and they do offer English speaking courses at University of Iceland. I have dreamed of going to Iceland for long, so that was the main reason I chose this destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was great, only would have wished I went on more trips and partied more!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say fairly easy, and if I could not find the information myself I could always email either KU or the University of Iceland.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a mentor. I only met with my mentor one time, but I could always write her if I had a question. There is a help desk at the main building at university where they help students getting a student ID and so on. I could also write teachers to ask about courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
When I arrived, numbers of Covid cases rose so most of the orientation was canceled or made online, which of course was a disappointment, but also understandable. Students wanting to go abroad, no matter where they go, should be aware and accept that this might and probably will happen.

I think the mentoring program could have been better. They talked about arranging trips around Iceland for exchange students, but there were no trips as far as I know. This was a bit disappointing. I think a lot of the socializing I had to do myself, it was not like they had a lot of events I could go to and thereby meet people. So this was a bit tough, but I found good friends myself. 

They have good student support of you reach out though - it is possible to attend mindfulness classes and they also have a therapist that you can book an appointment with if you need that.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky to find it in a post on the Facebook side that the University created for new students arriving. I know many others have found their accomondation through the website "housing anywhere". I got offered student housing, but by then I had already signed the other lease. When I created my profile for student housing, I had a very high number on the list so I thought I would never receive an offer, but in the end I did. So I think it is possible to get student housing even if you apply late, but you will need to be patient and to be okay with waiting for signing a lease until very late. There are other Facebook groups where you can find rooms for rent as well.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in a house with other flatmates. I liked it a lot since I got the opportunity to engage with other people than just exchange students, and also to live in down town, so where all the bars and shops are, which was really nice. I paid 95.000 ISK per month, which is about 4.800 DKK. I think you can get it a bit cheaper other places, but it is in that price range often, especially if you want to live in central Reykjavík.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I visited friends living in student housing, and it looks really nice. In Gamli Gardur there are mostly just exchange students, so there are many parties and people who wants to hang out. The rooms are very nice, Scandinavian design and new.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very easy. If you only stay one semester you just have to go to the help desk and say you have arrived, and you apply for a student card. I got a kennintala, which is like a CPR number because I moved my address to Iceland. That is very easy too, you just go to Registers Iceland and they register you. The number you also use when you go to the doctor, if you get a job and so on.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: At the help desk they told me to go to Registers Iceland to get a Kennintala. I could also email the international devision to get answers to my questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
They have a good system where it is possible 15 days after classes have started that one can change courses. This is all done online. I had to do this since two classes overlapped.
One thing that makes it slightly difficult is that they have a min. 60 % rule. It means that at least 60 % of your courses (so 20 ects) has to be in one school/faculty. So you can't just choose random courses. Therefore I ended up taking a course I did not really want, but the other courses I wanted were online, and I did not want any online courses. Courses within one faculty, for instance humanities, do mostly not overlap, but if you take courses within different faculties they might overlap, and then you have to re-elect courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the min 60 % rule.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There is more work during the semester than at KU. Less reading, but more tests that count towards your final grade. I had tests in all of my subjects, so I always had to do some kind of work. The texts I read was easier than at KU. I think my courses did not go so much in depht as the courses at KU. The exam was easier than exams at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had teaching in class and traditional lectures. This was a lot like how it is at KU, but perhaps a little less formal.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ENS 101G How Language Works I: Sound and Word (5 ects)
ENS 102G The Talking Animal (5 ects)
ÞJÓ 506G Performance Studies (10 ects)
ÍSE 025G Icelandic - the Basics (10 ects)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Performance Studies and Icelandic - the Basics. 
The teacher in performance studies is one of the best one I have had. He cares so much for his students and for the course. Gives great feedback and is a fun and great teacher. Take it if you like theatre, dance, music and theories about how everything we do can be seen as a performance. You will go on small field work trips by yourself which is also cool. 

I would also recommend Icelandic - the Basics if you would like to learn Icelandic. It is fun and I am happy I learned some Icelandic because it made me  feel more like home, and it is also cool to be able to go to stores and actually be able to communicate in Icelandic. The teaching is good too and I would say as a Danish speaker it will not be that difficult to learn Icelandic, even though they have cases in their grammar.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My hiking boots needed fixing which costed 1100 DKK

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Public transportation is cheap. Taking the bus anywhere for 1 hour and 15 minutes costs 25 DKK. 
Cheese is very expensive. 
Sodas and some candies are cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The public outside pools are amazing - cheap and so cozy.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a gym and a sauna at university which only costs 250 DKK for half a year. They also had some dance classes I did not attend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Going to the pool 
Knit - I met knitting friends at Kex hostel, where they have different events, here also a knitting event. 
Become friends with other exchange students and hang out

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out and see the wonders of Icelandic nature. Rent a car or take the bus somewhere. Go to the pools, either the public once or Sky Lagoon that is a bit more luxiurious.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
The culture is kind of like the Danish culture. I did not find it easy to get Icelandic friends, so I think you really need to work for this if you want Icelandic friends too.
I would say that there is a good relationship between Denmark and Iceland, but remember that Iceland used to be a Danish colony, so you might get a comment or two about this when you tell people that you are Danish. People still learn Danish at school, but few can really speak it, and also many do not like having to learn Danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you have classes with Icelanders, talk with them instead of just chatting with exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
It was difficult to get Icelandic friends. 
It is not easy to bicycle in Reykjavík, which I missed to do a lot.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That everyone goes to the pool to hang out - it is kind of like going to a park in Copenhagen to chat with friends.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Bring warm clothes 
- It is useful to have a drivers license, but if you do not, just find some friends that have so you can go on road trips
- Find a job so you can afford more trips and go more out. Also it is a great way to get to know more people

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take lots of Vitamin D

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a bunch of new people and experiencing the nature. Going on horse back riding trips.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling lonely and being homesick in the beginning. It wears off, but it happened to me hard in the beginning

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Just go! You won't regret it. 
I felt pretty safe staying in Iceland considering Covid. Not many people live there so it felt safe, and it was easy to get quick tests if needed.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
